root.name: Caro-Kann Defense: Tartakower Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 dxe4 4. Nxe4 Nf6 5. Nxf6+ exf6

overview: Black recaptures with the e-pawn, accepting doubled f-pawns for an open e-file and free development of the light bishop (this is the Bronstein-Larsen set-up). After 6.c3 Bd6 7.Bd3 Black develops with ...Qc7, ...Be6 and ...Nd7, king in the centre or castled short, against a White with a small space edge and chances against the f6/f7 structure.

white_ideas.idea: Play c3, Bd3, Qe2+ and Ne2/Nf3, aiming at the e-file and the weakened f-pawns.
Exploit the doubled f-pawns with quick development and target the king.

black_ideas.idea: Develop ...Bd6, ...Qc7, ...Be6, ...Nd7 and castle, using the e-file and the bishop pair potential.
Use the open e-file and ...f5 later to free the position and play for activity.

typical_structures.structure: Black with doubled f-pawns (f7, f6) and an open e-file; White with c3/d4 chain.

character.notes: Sound and defensible but with a damaged structure; Black has to avoid being pushed around, yet there are few quick losses.

gambit.notes: All captures are recaptures; no material is offered.

structure.notes: Symmetrical-ish exchange of the e-pawn gives a half-open e-file; centre not locked.

level.notes: Black must handle the doubled pawns and piece activity; no long forcing lines.

sublines_that_differ.name: 6.Bc4
sublines_that_differ.how: Sharper, with exchanges and rapid development.

character.reason: Caro-Kann structure is hard to break down despite the doubled pawns.

structure.reason: Half-open e-file for Black, pawn centre not locked.

level.reason: Understanding the doubled-pawn structure matters more than memory.

plans.reason: Black's doubled f-pawns define the position.
